candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 14:1 (Abraham cycle (14:1)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'After these things, in the fourth year of this week, on the new moon of the third month, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a dream, saying: Fear not, Abram, I am thy defender, and thy reward will be exceeding great' — Jubilees uniquely dates the covenant-of-pieces vision to the new moon of the third month, the date that becomes Pentecost (Jub 6:17). The Tewahedo Pentecost (Pärräqlēṭos, fiftieth day) thus has a TRIPLE canonical anchor: Noah's covenant (Jub 6:17), Abram's covenant (Jub 14:1), and Sinai (Ex 19) — three covenant-moments on the same calendar date. The covenant-renewal liturgy of the Tewahedo Pentecost commemorates all three jointly.

candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 14:13 (Abraham cycle (14:13)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'Take Me an heifer of three years, and a goat of three years, and a sheep of three years, and a turtle-dove and a pigeon' — the covenant-cutting sacrifice is enumerated. Jubilees emphasizes the threefold age (three years) of each large animal as cosmic-completeness symbol (parallel to the threefold sevens of jubilee reckoning). Tewahedo liturgical-numerology preserves this triadic symbolism: the threefold offering at the altar (bread + wine + incense), the threefold psalmody at the daily office (matins + sext + vespers), and the threefold theological framing of every Anaphora (creation + redemption + sanctification) all draw canonical warrant from the threefold animal-offering of Abram.

candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 14:18 (Abraham cycle (14:18)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And on that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying: To thy seed will I give this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates' — Jubilees preserves the land-promise within the covenant of pieces. The Tewahedo reading distinguishes the land promise to ethnic Israel (literal fulfilment from Joshua through the divided monarchy) from the universalized land promise to Abram's spiritual seed (the Tewahedo Church inherits the promise as the elected community of those who keep the covenant by faith — cf. Gal 3:7-9, an apostolic reading the Tewahedo retains against any 'Christ-against-Israel' supersessionist framework). The canonical doubled land-witness in Jubilees + Genesis is the warrant for the broad inheritance.

candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 14:21 (Abraham cycle (14:21)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Abram rejoiced and told all these things to Sarai his wife; and he believed that he should have a seed, but she did not bear' — Jubilees notes Abram's verbal sharing of the covenant with Sarai, an inclusion of the matriarch absent from the Genesis parallel. Tewahedo Marian theology reads this inclusion as the canonical precedent for full-disclosure of revelation to women: the matriarch is the legitimate hearer of covenant. The Tewahedo elaboration of the Wǝddase Maryam (Praise of Mary) draws on Sarai's reception-of-covenant-by-her-husband's-report as the type of Mary's fiat — the woman who receives the covenant news and consents.

'After these things, in the fourth year of this week, on the new moon of the third month, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a dream, saying: Fear not, Abram, I am thy defender, and thy reward will be exceeding great' — Jubilees uniquely dates the covenant-of-pieces vision to the new moon of the third month, the date that becomes Pentecost (Jub 6:17). The Tewahedo Pentecost (Pärräqlēṭos, fiftieth day) thus has a TRIPLE canonical anchor: Noah's covenant (Jub 6:17), Abram's covenant (Jub 14:1), and Sinai (Ex 19) — three covenant-moments on the same calendar date. The covenant-renewal liturgy of the Tewahedo Pentecost commemorates all three jointly.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'Take Me an heifer of three years, and a goat of three years, and a sheep of three years, and a turtle-dove and a pigeon' — the covenant-cutting sacrifice is enumerated. Jubilees emphasizes the threefold age (three years) of each large animal as cosmic-completeness symbol (parallel to the threefold sevens of jubilee reckoning). Tewahedo liturgical-numerology preserves this triadic symbolism: the threefold offering at the altar (bread + wine + incense), the threefold psalmody at the daily office (matins + sext + vespers), and the threefold theological framing of every Anaphora (creation + redemption + sanctification) all draw canonical warrant from the threefold animal-offering of Abram.

candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 14:18 (Abraham cycle (14:18)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And on that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying: To thy seed will I give this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates' — Jubilees preserves the land-promise within the covenant of pieces. The Tewahedo reading distinguishes the land promise to ethnic Israel (literal fulfilment from Joshua through the divided monarchy) from the universalized land promise to Abram's spiritual seed (the Tewahedo Church inherits the promise as the elected community of those who keep the covenant by faith — cf. Gal 3:7-9, an apostolic reading the Tewahedo retains against any 'Christ-against-Israel' supersessionist framework). The canonical doubled land-witness in Jubilees + Genesis is the warrant for the broad inheritance.

candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 14:21 (Abraham cycle (14:21)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Abram rejoiced and told all these things to Sarai his wife; and he believed that he should have a seed, but she did not bear' — Jubilees notes Abram's verbal sharing of the covenant with Sarai, an inclusion of the matriarch absent from the Genesis parallel. Tewahedo Marian theology reads this inclusion as the canonical precedent for full-disclosure of revelation to women: the matriarch is the legitimate hearer of covenant. The Tewahedo elaboration of the Wǝddase Maryam (Praise of Mary) draws on Sarai's reception-of-covenant-by-her-husband's-report as the type of Mary's fiat — the woman who receives the covenant news and consents.
